i built lgtmaybe, an open-source code reviewer, and a lot of the work went into making it usable on a local model. Big files get reviewed a hunk at a time, and big diffs get split to fit the context window, so a 27B model copes fine. The default is five model calls per review, which is fine on one GPU. In llama.cpp / mixed-quant repos, BF16 PLE sidecars (~95 GiB, mmap from SSD) are real and people measure a clear quality win. In Strata, the supported “don’t quantize the table hard” upgrade is --ple-gguf → FP8 (or Q8_0), not a documented BF16 95 GB GGUF loader. So: take the comment seriously (don’t run with IQ4_NL PLE if you care about quality), but on Strata implement it as FP8 or Q8_0 via --ple-gguf, not by hunting for a BF16 file unless you confirm your exact Strata version accepts BF16 PLE rows.

Ha, finally some engineering talk. The original design was for en-grams to be fully stored in RAM, in practice it turns out as you say the call distribution is wildly lopsided unlike with experts in MoE models, so storing a fraction in RAM is more practical for scaled down use. In my own testing for example I found you can trivially store the image encoder in RAM, for the occasional image in a prompt you lose barely a few ms in encode, in return you free up VRAM without turning your model blind.

The fruit is quite low hanging for optimisations here.

comfyui requires you to have knowledge on how diffusion models work. like if you literally take a course or do some self study, it becomes much clearer. otherwise it's a jumble of variables and spaghetti lines that nobody explains anywhere. i was its worst hater several years ago, now i think it's pretty okay. at the very least, you might wanna ask an llm about how to use it and what some of the variables mean. Unlike llm serving which has been nicely simplified for the end user now, comfyui is designed to allow the user to define what the inputs and outputs are with much more flexibility. it's closer to n8n if you know what that is.

i also agree with the other commenter that you're probably looking at the slop workflows in the first place. the default templates with 5 boxes and lines work out of the box. whatever huge workflow you're looking at, you can treat it like a badly vibecoded pr to llama.cpp. might do something neat, no guarantee to work at all on your hardware.
